meta: Aqua HK spent HK$9,477 on Meta for 19 schedules, about HK$499 each. That is better than HK$699 for 11 schedules the week before, but still outside the good band, and spend rose 23.3 percent to the highest Meta week of the eight here.
Dim Sum Library spent HK$1,058 for 4 schedules, roughly HK$265 each. That is inside the good band and level with HK$266 the week before, on a very small and steady base.
Meta remains a thin last-click channel in Hong Kong: 23 combined schedules against 374 GA4 bookings across these two venues, so read the spend as awareness rather than acquisition.
google: Aqua HK Google ran HK$8,084 for about 48 booking conversions at roughly HK$167 CPA, just outside the good band, against 44 conversions on HK$9,683 the week before. Spend came down 16.5 percent and conversions rose 11 percent, so the CPA improved by a quarter.
Dim Sum Library Google delivered about 58 conversions on HK$1,514 at roughly HK$26 CPA, still the cheapest acquisition in the portfolio, against 63 conversions on HK$1,316 the week before.
Brand search carried the volume at both venues, 29 of 48 conversions at Aqua HK and 35 of 58 at Dim Sum Library. Read these as existing name demand rather than new reach.
ga4: Aqua HK users fell 6.7 percent week on week to 3,662 and are 13.3 percent below last year, while conversion rose to 5.6 percent from 4.5 percent. Bookings of 206 are 10.8 percent below last year and 18.3 percent under the weekly target. The recovery here is conversion, not traffic.

Dim Sum Library users rose 4.9 percent week on week to 1,035 and are 16.4 percent below last year, while conversion improved to 16.2 percent from 13.8 percent. Bookings of 168 are the best of the eight weeks and up 23.5 percent, yet still 8.7 percent below last year and 9.7 percent below the weekly target, so the gap here is traffic volume rather than conversion.
These remain the only two Hong Kong venues behind on the FY-to-date line, Aqua HK by 6.2 percent and Dim Sum Library by 8.9 percent. The other four are all ahead.
